newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pension fund payments and rising operating costs plunged Transnet into a loss of 253 million rand for the year ended March.

- The task team responsible for rewriting South Africa's competition policy appears to have thrown out the U.S. anti-trust model in favour of a mixture of British and Canadian competition law, sources say.
- A new 520 million rand steel rolling mill at Saldanha is being considered by the Industrial Development Corp in a joint-venture with Dorbyl's Baldwin Steel and Swiss steel trader Duferco.
- Investigations of recent violence at Goldfields's East Driefontein mine pointed to a "third force or criminal interest" was fanning ethnic conflict, SAPS Captain Eugene Potgieter said.
- Transnet, the transport parastatal, moved 253 million rand into the red in the year to March 31 from a profit of 118 million rand last year.

- The debate in the U.S. as to whether interest rates would rise over the next few months is threatening to complicate the South African government's roadshow next month to promote its planned sale of dollar-denominated bonds, a European banking official said.
- The battle for market share between South Africa's fridge makers could escalate over the coming year, industry sources said.

- Anglo American Properties , one of the biggest property owners in Johannesburg's Central Business District (CBD), expects its city portfolio to be 50 percent vacant next year as the exodus from the CBD continues unabated.
- A cache of explosives, traditional weapons, guns and ammunition and a large amount of dagga were found in a swoop by police and soldiers on a hostel at the Buffelsfontein mine.
- Sonja Combrink was convicted of kidnapping Micaela Hunter, but sentencing was postponed until November 18.
- A manhunt that extended all the way to Cape Town was launched by police after the gruesome murder of two women and a toddler by robbers in the Northern Cape hamlet of Nieuwoudtville.
